utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-PT, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the appearances, please. The Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour; good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Mr. David Re on my right-hand side, Ms. Kimberly Fleming as the case manager, and I, Ekkehard Withopf, Senior Trial Attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Mr. Ibrisimovic. With me is Mr. Rodney Dixon and our case assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Kubura, would you rise, please. Can you hear the interpretation? THE ACCUSED KUBURA: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please identify yourself, please. THE ACCUSED KUBURA: [Interpretation] Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your date of birth, please. THE ACCUSED KUBURA: [Interpretation] The 4th of March, 1964, in Kakanj, the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And your address? THE ACCUSED KUBURA: [Interpretation] I live in Sarajevo, Topalosman-Pase number 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated. This hearing is held in accordance with Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and the Prosecution, in its motion of the 15th of August, required an amendment to the indictment, and by ruling of the 17th of September 2003, the Chamber determined that the Prosecutor may present a new indictment against you. Actually, this has to do with facts related to the killing of four HVO soldiers whose names appear in paragraph 39, and this was committed on the 29th of April, 1993. So it's count number 1, murder, violations of the rules and customs of war. You have, therefore, been informed of this new charge. Your counsel addressed a letter to the Chamber noting that it had been informed of this amendment, so I will now ask you to rise and to tell me whether you personally have been informed of this new charge. THE ACCUSED KUBURA: [Interpretation] Yes, I have. Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So my question to you now regarding this new count: Do you plead guilty or not guilty? THE ACCUSED KUBURA: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty on this count.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I take note of the fact that you have pleaded not guilty of this new count in the indictment. You may be seated. There are no other comments regarding this additional initial appearance, due to which this hearing is closed. We will now adjourn and resume in a few minutes. But I see that the Prosecutor wishes to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. There was an additional new charge. That's paragraph 44. That's wanton destruction for Miletici. This concerns count 5 and count 6. We added Miletici to the list of the areas in which destruction took place, destruction committed by the subordinates of the accused Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. The Prosecutor is indicating that in paragraph 44, there is the charge of wanton destruction of buildings committed in Miletici appearing under count 5 and 6. Has the Defence any observations to make in that connection?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No observations, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Kubura, will you rise, please. You heard the Prosecution telling us of a charge of wanton destruction under counts 5 and 6 having to do with destruction of facilities and buildings in Miletici. Do you have any comments to make, and do you plead guilty or not guilty of this crime? THE ACCUSED KUBURA: [Interpretation] I have heard, and I also plead not guilty regarding this count.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was referring not only to count 5 in the indictment but also to count 6, plunder of public and private property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. There is destruction and plunder, counts 5 and 6. No comments by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, this hearing is adjourned. There's an intervention on behalf of the Defence. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we were just saying that we have no observations regarding the statement by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This hearing is adjourned. We will resume in a few minutes with the two accused for the 65 ter hearing. Do you wish to intervene again, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: It is our understanding, Your Honour, that the accused Kubura has not yet pled to count 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Kubura, the Prosecutor has noted that he didn't quite gather whether you pleaded guilty or not guilty regarding count 6, plunder. So I'm asking you once again: Are you pleading guilty or not guilty regarding plunder? THE ACCUSED KUBURA: [Interpretation] I plead not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the understanding of the Chamber too. Thank you. Please be seated. So we will have a few minutes' break to be able to change the tape, and we will resume the pre-trial hearing shortly.
